paper_sections.title: Aging of visual word perception is related to decreased segregation within and beyond the word network in the brain
Data preprocessing for resting-state fMRI data
Between-group difference of behavioral performances in visual matching task
Between-group difference in resting-state functional connectivity

description.value: The study examined age-related differences in visual word perception, resting-state functional connectivity within the word network and beyond it, and relationships between connectivity and visual word-matching performance.

design.value: The study recruited healthy older and young adults, collected resting-state and task fMRI data, identified word-selective ventral occipitotemporal regions using a block-designed word localizer, and subsequently assessed visual word and symbol-form matching behavior.

description.value: The Chinese version of the standardized assessment was used for evaluating non-verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) and general cognitive ability.
Participants determined whether two visually presented words were identical, with inverse efficiency score calculated as average correct reaction time divided by proportion of correct responses.
A baseline control test using the same procedure as the word matching test, with symbol-form stimuli.
19 healthy older adults; all participants were right-handed individuals with no history of encephalopathy or mental illness and exhibited normal vision.

exclusion_criteria.value: no history of encephalopathy or mental illness

education_summary.value: Both groups had completed their junior high school or higher education. The older adults had a mean of 12.60 years of schooling (SD = 2.74).

description.value: 22 young adults; all participants were right-handed individuals with no history of encephalopathy or mental illness and exhibited normal vision.

exclusion_criteria.value: no history of encephalopathy or mental illness

education_summary.value: Both groups had completed their junior high school or higher education. The young adults had a mean of 15.89 years of schooling (SD = 1.54).

task_description.value: A block-designed localizer task in which participants judged whether visual stimuli appeared on the left or right side of the fixation point.

instructions.value: Participants judged the location of the stimulus by pressing the corresponding button as accurately and quickly as possible.

stimuli.value: Chinese characters and phase-separated Chinese characters; each picture was presented for 250 ms, followed by a 750-ms inter-stimulus interval.

task_description.value: Participants rested in a quiet state during resting-state fMRI data collection.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to rest adequately the day before the experiment and keep their heads as still as possible during the scan.

task_description.value: Participants performed word matching and symbol-form matching tasks involving same/different judgments.

instructions.value: Participants had to quickly determine whether the two words on the screen were identical and press the corresponding button as swiftly and accurately as possible.

stimuli.value: 30 new pictures of words and 30 new pictures of symbols, all in stick figure style.

task_performance_measures.value: inverse efficiency score (IES), calculated as the average correct reaction time divided by the proportion of correct responses

instrument.value: GE 3-Tesla MRI scanner (MR-750, GE Medical Systems, Milwaukee, WI)

description.value: Echo Planar Imaging (EPI) was used to obtain resting-state and task-fMRI data. The imaging parameters were 43 axial slices, flip angle 90°, field of view 220 × 220 mm², and matrix size 64 × 64. The resting session comprised 240 contiguous volumes, lasting 8 min, followed by the task localizer session, which lasted 8 min and 10 s.

number_of_volumes.value: 240 resting-state volumes; 245 total continuous time points

description.value: Task-fMRI data were preprocessed using DPABI. The preprocessing steps were removal of the first five time points, slice timing, realignment, spatial normalization to the EPI template in MNI space, and spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with FWHM of 6 mm.

software.value: Data Processing and Analysis for Brain Imaging (DPABI) toolkit, based on MATLAB

steps.value: removal of the first five time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space
spatial smoothing using an isotropic Gaussian kernel with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 6 mm

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were preprocessed using the DPABI toolkit.

steps.value: removal of the first 10 time points
spatial normalization to the EPI template in MNI space
regression of covariates including head motion profiles (Friston 24-parameter), white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals

model_settings.value: The phase-scattered Chinese characters were used as a baseline in the localizer task, and activation levels caused by Chinese character images were compared. The linear contrast image was Chinese characters vs. scattered Chinese characters.

estimator.value: one-sample t-test for the group-level activation map

model_settings.value: Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between averaged ROI time courses or between each ROI time course and every voxel in the brain, followed by Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.

estimator.value: Pearson correlation coefficient with Fisher’s r-to-z transformation; two-sample t-tests for between-group differences

description.value: Participants were scanned in a quiet state.
Visual stimuli consisting of Chinese character images.
Phase-scattered Chinese characters used as the baseline in the localizer task.
Word stimuli in the visual word-matching task.
Symbol-form stimuli used as the baseline control condition.
